chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The cutting of the foot of the thief after the cutting of the hand, then it is not cut afterwards. So if he repeats, he is imprisoned, and he is provided for from the public treasury of the Muslims.
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a thief who commits theft more than once according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'no further amputation' (la yuqtadu ba'du) for repeat offenders, shifting the penalty from corporal punishment to incarceration and state maintenance (infāq). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the hadd of cutting is strictly limited to the first instance, with subsequent crimes handled via ta'zir or imprisonment, ensuring the thief's sustenance from the bayt al-mal.
